---
title: "Contribute"
---

There are four ways in, from least to most technical. All of them end with a pull request
that someone reviews before it goes live.

::: {.section-label}
Option 1: no git at all
:::

[Open an issue using the "Add a project" form](https://github.com/CasparDP/airbeitskreis/issues/new?template=add-project.yml).
Fill in four fields. A maintainer turns it into a pull request. This is the right choice if
the words "pull request" already sound like work.

::: {.section-label}
Option 2: the GitHub web interface
:::

Everything below happens in a browser. Nothing to install, no Quarto, no command line.

**To link to something you already published elsewhere**, a blog post, a repository, a
paper, edit
[`projects/links.yml`](https://github.com/CasparDP/airbeitskreis/edit/main/projects/links.yml)
and append an entry:

```yaml
- title: "Grading 120 theses with a rubric agent"
  description: "One sentence. This is the only text shown on the card."
  author: "Your Name"
  date: "2026-07-22"
  categories: [teaching]
  tools: [claude-code]
  path: "https://your-site.example/the-post"
```

**To write a full page on this site instead**, copy
[`projects/_template.qmd`](https://github.com/CasparDP/airbeitskreis/blob/main/projects/_template.qmd),
rename it to something like `my-project.qmd`, and edit it. The template has the frontmatter
filled in and section headings to write against.

Either way, GitHub will offer to open a pull request when you save. Take it.

::: {.section-label}
Option 3: locally
:::

```bash
git clone https://github.com/CasparDP/airbeitskreis.git
cd airbeitskreis
quarto preview                      # live reload; Quarto prints the URL

# The schema check CI runs. Needs pyyaml, so use a throwaway virtual environment:
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install pyyaml
.venv/bin/python scripts/validate_projects.py
```

::: {.section-label}
Option 4: let an agent do it
:::

The repository carries the contribution procedure as an agent skill, so if you already work
in an AI coding tool you can hand it the job. Clone the repository, open it in your agent,
and describe your project in plain language.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/CasparDP/airbeitskreis.git
cd airbeitskreis
claude        # then: "add my project to this site: ..."
```

Claude Code picks up `.claude/skills/add-project/SKILL.md` on its own. Other tools read
`AGENTS.md` in the repository root, which points at the same file. The agent asks for
whatever it still needs, writes the entry, runs the same checks CI runs, and opens the pull
request.

It is the slowest way to add a one-line link and the only one that is also a demonstration
of the thing this site is about. Read the diff before you approve it: the agent is good at
the format and cannot know what you actually did.

::: {.section-label}
The fields
:::

Both entry types use the same fields.

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | yes | Specific and concrete. "Grading 120 theses with a rubric agent" beats "Using AI for grading". |
| `description` | yes | One sentence. The only text on the card. |
| `author` | yes | As you want to be credited. |
| `date` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `categories` | yes | From the fixed list below. |
| `tools` | no | From the fixed list below. Shown on the card. |
| `image` | no | Path to a thumbnail, e.g. `/images/my-thumb.png`. Landscape works best (the card crops it to a wide strip). Leave it out and the card shows the A(I) monogram tile. |
| `path` | link entries only | Absolute `https://` URL. Leave it out entirely for full pages. |

**Categories** (pick one or more): `teaching`, `research`, `writing`, `data`, `admin`,
`tools`, `fun`.

**Tools** (pick any that apply): `claude`, `claude-code`, `chatgpt`, `codex`, `copilot`,
`ollama`, `lm-studio`.

Both lists are deliberately closed, so the filters stay useful instead of fragmenting into
forty near-duplicates. Anything outside them fails CI with a message naming the problem. To
add a value to either list, open a PR changing `scripts/validate_projects.py` and this page.

::: {.section-label}
One rule about code
:::

Project pages are prose by default. If your page needs to *execute* R or Python, set
`freeze: auto` in its frontmatter and commit the generated `_freeze/` directory. CI renders
the site without installing anyone's packages, so an unfrozen `library(fixest)` would break
deploys for everyone.

::: {.section-label}
What happens next
:::

CI renders your PR and validates your entry. A maintainer reviews it. On merge, the site
rebuilds and your project is live within a couple of minutes.
